question: Roughly how many nerve cells line the human gut?
answer: Hundreds of millions, more than in the spinal cord, forming the enteric nervous system, which runs digestion largely on its own. Enders calls it a gut brain: it signals to the brain in the head through the vagus nerve, one reason worry and digestion so often travel together.
move: Digestion runs on its own nervous system, which talks to your brain.
trap: 'A few thousand': a tube seems to need little wiring.
simply: Your gut has its own web of nerves, bigger than the one in your spine. It runs digestion and talks to your brain all day.
why: It helps explain why stress upsets the stomach and a bad stomach can sour the mood: the two are wired together, so caring for one often helps the other.
reference: Giulia Enders, Gut: The Inside Story of Our Body's Most Underrated Organ (Greystone Books, 2015), ch. 2
